sections.heading: Overview
bullets: A maze traverse, not a fight — navigate the shifting castle to reach Xera while managing a stacking madness effect. No gliding here; falling usually means death.

sections.heading: Madness stacks
bullets: Everyone gains Madness stacks steadily just from being in the castle, building faster while you're looking at the giant rotating statue in the center — don't stare at it.

Effects escalate in steps: 10/20 stacks cripple you (longer each time), 30 stacks deals heavy damage if you're facing the spire, 40/70 stacks apply Torment, 60 stacks deals even heavier damage if facing the spire, 80/90 stacks apply Fear, and 99 stacks is an instant kill with no exceptions.
Fountains scattered through the castle cleanse 10 stacks at a time ("dip your hands") — prefer that over "drink the water," which only pauses the buildup instead of removing it.

sections.heading: Haunting Statues
bullets: They chase anyone who isn't maintaining eye contact with them. You can't damage them, but you can knock, pull, or push them — walking into one teleports you back to the start of the route, so treat them as a hard obstacle, not a fight.

sections.heading: The route
bullets: Clear the starter platform, take the left portal down a damaging staircase, then the southwest portal to a U-shaped platform with mobs.
Dodge off the U-shaped platform onto the lower archway — stay at full health before this jump, it's punishing.
Hit buttons 3 and 4, then head left past statues and White Mantle enemies, jump the rocky sections, and climb the staircases to the final door.
White Mantle enemies here knock back and knock down — watch your footing near platform edges.

Pink one-way teleport gates take priority over player-placed portals, and only activate once every enemy on that platform is cleared — don't rely on a Mesmer portal to skip past a gate that hasn't opened yet.
There are 7 door-button pairs scattered through the castle; the final door only needs 5 of them activated, so don't feel obligated to find every single one.
Some floor panels are fake (a subtle distortion effect) and drop you to your death — look before you jump on an unfamiliar section.
